scenes.text: this is the loneliest spot on Earth.
Deep in the South Pacific lies Point Nemo, the ocean's pole of inaccessibility.
First, it sits about 1,670 miles from the nearest piece of land.
While Finding Nemo made 871 million dollars, real Nemo means no one.
Second, when the Space Station passes directly overhead, astronauts are only 258 miles up.
They are six times closer to Point Nemo than any human on land.
Third, space agencies use this watery desert as a giant spacecraft graveyard.
Over 260 spacecraft have been crashed here, with the Space Station joining them.
